teams.heading: Jake White will move to live in Fiji in early 2027
teams.body: Fiji coach Jake White, who led South Africa to 2007 World Cup glory, told The42 before Saturday's Dublin test that he will spend blocks of each year touring the islands. The Fiji U18 and U20 squads will start touring South Africa every year, and White plans to coach in schools and clubs, seeing a need to supplement Fiji's traditional culture of flair. "No one mauls in Fiji," he says, and nobody coaches it.

lead.why: White's interview gives the freshest Fiji-side detail in the pack, covering his move to Fiji, his grassroots plans and his views on the Fiji game, beyond the Ireland-travel call already reported.

teams.heading: Will Joseph scored five tries as England beat Japan 78-15
teams.body: Twickenham on Saturday produced 13 England tries, five of them from Will Joseph, who was rated 10/10 in one outlet's player ratings. England head coach Steve Borthwick told ITV afterwards he would "praise the bench" and that "they were great", after a match in which viewers' complaints centred on ITV's in-game adverts rather than the rugby itself, which drew no complaints.

lead.why: A new event from Saturday's match, a five-try haul by Will Joseph, rather than the Australia win already covered.

teams.heading: Julien Marchand ruled out for rest of Nations Championship as Jalibert nears return
teams.body: Julien Marchand has been ruled out for the rest of the Nations Championship, Planet Rugby reports, after thigh tightness during the warm-up before Friday's win over South Africa. Peato Mauvaka started in his place, and Guillaume Cramont will be reserve hooker for the Argentina match and the finals. The news is partly offset by Matthieu Jalibert, who has not played since September with a quadriceps injury and is expected at the Marcoussis camp early next week.

lead.why: It is a fresh France team-news event, an injury ruling-out for the rest of the competition, and the most practical story for the Argentina match.

teams.heading: Andy Farrell restored Jamison Gibson-Park as Ireland made seven changes against Fiji
teams.body: Injuries to Dan Sheehan and Sean Jansen forced two of Saturday's changes, while Joe McCarthy and Hugo Keenan were rested from the matchday squad. Jamison Gibson-Park returns as first-choice scrum-half, James Ryan and Tommy O'Brien come in, and Mack Hansen starts at fullback. The 42 judged the team less of an experiment than the number suggests, with James McNabney, Sam Illo and Darragh Murray adding depth on the bench before the South Africa match next week.

lead.why: It is the only fresh Ireland event on the shortlist, a named selection decision with specific personnel changes.

teams.heading: Paolo Garbisi misses late penalty touch kick as Argentina edge Italy 19-14
teams.body: Italy fly-half Paolo Garbisi missed a penalty touch kick in the closing moments of Saturday's Genoa test, the attempt meant to set up a lineout in a scoring position, and Argentina held on to win 19-14. Italy had been reduced to 14 men after substitute lock Efrain Elias was shown a yellow card, yet a penalty try had brought them back within five points after winger Monty Ioane's early try. Planet Rugby noted that Garbisi had the chance to clinch a first victory over Argentina in 18 years.

lead.why: It is a fresh, match-defining moment that Italy fans will be talking about, and it is covered in more than one outlet.

teams.heading: Joey Sharp, five, to deliver Murrayfield match ball before Scotland-Australia test
teams.body: Joey Sharp, who was diagnosed with a brain tumour at 11 days old, will deliver the match ball alongside Commonwealth Games swimmer Archie Goodburn, a brain tumour research campaigner. Scottish Rugby have arranged for Joey and his mother, Sam Sharp, to meet the players and have provided accessible seating. "He's looking forward to the day out," Ms Sharp said, adding that Joey, from Penicuik, had been too unwell to attend before.

lead.why: It is the freshest new item with two outlets behind it, and it is a Scotland story about the team's matchday, not a preview or a repeat of Tuipulotu's comments.

teams.heading: James Botham and Jac Morgan spearhead Wales defence that repelled All Blacks
teams.body: Saturday's 35-28 win over New Zealand was settled as much at the back as in attack. With New Zealand flanker Peter Lakai's late try cutting the margin to seven, Wales' defenders held firm in the final quarter, and WalesOnline described the effort as miraculous, with Gareth Thomas, James Botham, Jac Morgan, Dafydd Jenkins and Eddie James all singled out. Wales made more than 300 tackles, and the All Blacks had 65 per cent of the possession, according to Planet Rugby.

lead.why: It moves the story from the result to the defensive effort that held the win together, a Wales-specific angle the other candidates don't develop.

teams.heading: Felipe Contepomi credits Pumas' character after 19-14 Genoa win over Italy
teams.body: Felipe Contepomi said the Pumas' 19-14 win in Genoa rested on character rather than control, with his side scoring a first-half try while a man down after a yellow card. The Argentina coach conceded that Italy had dominated possession and territory in the first half, stressing that in these matches converting and scoring is what counts. He described a squad still in construction, with two weeks together ahead of the trip to France.

lead.why: It is the newest item in the pack, a post-match verdict from Argentina's coach on the Genoa win, and it looks ahead to the France match.

teams.heading: Carter Gordon recalled at flyhalf as Les Kiss restores Rob Valetini
teams.body: Carter Gordon is back at No 10 for Sunday's clash with Scotland, and Australia coach Les Kiss sees him as the answer to a jersey that has had seven different starters since the last World Cup. Gordon is back from a broken leg and was building into the role before the Argentina injury. Rob Valetini returns at six, with Declan Meredith dropped from the match-day 23. "Certainly Carter was the incumbent, so he was in a position of strength before he got injured," Kiss said.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones vowed Japan would 'play the house down'; England won 78-15
teams.body: Japan coach Eddie Jones had vowed his side would 'play the house down' at Twickenham, but Japan were beaten 78-15 by England on Saturday. The Brave Blossoms had a player sent off before touching the ball, according to The Guardian, and England ran in 13 tries. The defeat leaves Japan with one win from five matches in the log, with Scotland next.

lead.why: It is the only new Japan item on the shortlist, and it gives the Saturday defeat a coaching angle.

teams.heading: Frank Bunce admitted he couldn't name a Welsh player before 35-28 defeat
teams.body: Bunce, the former All Blacks centre, told Sport Nation before the Cardiff test that he hadn't watched Wales much: "I couldn't name any of their players to be honest". He still expected New Zealand to win "whichever team we put out there", even after Dave Rennie made eight changes to the starting XV. Wales instead won 35-28 at the Principality Stadium, their first victory over the All Blacks since 1953, ending a 34-match losing run.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus says coaching staff must answer for Paris defeat to France
teams.body: Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus accepted responsibility after the 21-19 loss in Paris but kept circling back to the referee's position, describing the pressure Andrea Piardi faces before a partisan home crowd. He said the Boks may have asked too much of Piardi at the scrum, and that the side had been tentative, with the coaching staff needing to answer why. Erasmus stressed that France had played later the previous weekend and had less rest, saying: "I don't think there's much more to blame than ourselves."

lead.why: Erasmus's post-match press conference is a fresh, on-the-record admission that the coaching staff share the blame, which is new to the reader.
